points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (a tree in which each node has at most two children).

States the left-side ordering property: for any node, the left child is smaller than the parent (left child < parent). Accept equivalent wording such as 'all values in the left subtree are smaller than the node'.

States the right-side ordering property: for any node, the right child is greater than the parent (parent < right child). Accept equivalent wording such as 'all values in the right subtree are greater than the node'.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all three ideas: it is a binary tree, the left child is smaller than the parent, and the right child is greater than the parent, for every node. Award the binary-tree mark alone if only 'binary tree' is stated, and award the relevant inequality mark if only one side is correct. No marks for a plain binary tree with no ordering property, or if the inequalities are reversed.
